recorded_from_commit_note:
Recorded against this card's own implementation on its worktree, after the face swap and before any fixture was written, exactly as CARD-205's and CARD-200's recordings were. CARD-205's file is SUPERSEDED, NOT RE-RECORDED: that is a different card's deliberate ink change, which the chain's own rule (every baseline's 'warning' field) says gets a new file under its own card number. No earlier fixture in the chain is edited, regenerated or deleted by this card -- not even to add a superseded_by line (the practice CARD-149, CARD-146, CARD-147 and CARD-205 all followed for their own predecessors), and CARD-217's finding that the superseded recordings are referenced only from docstrings and cost no runtime is why there is nothing to gain by touching them.

RE-RECORDED IN PLACE ONCE, for this card's own fix cycle 1 -- a revision of this card's own fixture, not a new card superseding it, which is the same shape CARD-204 Fix 1 and CARD-205 Fix 2 used for their own re-recordings. The owner ruled on both of this card's open blocks on 2026-10-14 and neither by accepting the loss: (1) the guide page drops the difficulty box's three sentences, which buys 234 px against the 4 px that had cost page 2 its whole captions form, so the worked example's four step explanations and both technique notes are printed again -- the three sentences are the one block with a successor already carded (CARD-229 moves the difficulty legend into the guide's key strip); (2) TOC_GROUP_GAP_PT moves 8.5 -> 8.0 pt, which is the owner's own 'largest gap that fits, less a margin' rule re-measured on the packaged face (8.2 pt is the largest that fits; 8.0 leaves 6 px over the folio's line where 8.5 left -2). Measured page by page against this file's own pre-fix recording before it was rewritten: interior pages 2 and 3 move, and nothing else does.

why_a_new_baseline:
CARD-221 letters every reader-facing interior face in the PACKAGED font (src/nonogram/export/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf, the face the band and the folio were already set in) instead of resolving the HOST's Arial by path with Pillow's built-in face as a fallback. That is a deliberate change to what every lettered page prints, and it is made for a product reason rather than a tidiness one: the interior's row geometry was a function of what fonts the machine happened to have while the folio's own reservation was not, so the same book finalised on the owner's Mac and generated through the deployed Linux panel could disagree about its page count -- and the page count selects the printed KDP gutter band. Measured at Book 1's trim before the card: a TOC page held 42 rows on Arial and 40 on the fallback.

EXACTLY THE SEVEN PAGES THAT WERE LETTERED THROUGH _guide_face MOVED, AND NOTHING ELSE. Page-by-page digest comparison against CARD-205's recording, made before this file was written: pages 1 and 2 (the guide), 3 (the table of contents), 4, 6 and 8 (the level dividers) and 10 (the SOLUTIONS divider) are new; pages 5, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 13 (the two-up page, the two single-puzzle pages and the three answer pages) are byte-identical to CARD-205's own digests. Those six carry no _guide_face lettering at all -- a band, a caption and a folio are set in the packaged face and the clue digits in Pillow's own built-in one -- so a face swap cannot reach them, and the comparison says so rather than assuming it. That is the same list this file's predecessors recorded as font_dependent_pages, which is now empty for the reason below.

TWO MEASURED CONSEQUENCES THE CARD COULD NOT CLOSE, both because the packaged face is about a tenth wider than Arial at the same point size, and both escalated to the owner rather than papered over (see CARD-221's Worktree notes and the two strict xfail markers that carry the figures): (1) interior page 2 of THIS book -- the Book 1 trim -- drops from create_guide_page's captions form to its labels form, because one paragraph wraps into one more line and the captions form's last mark lands at 3192 px against a frame bottom of 3188. Four pixels, and the reader loses the worked example's four captions and the difficulty box's three sentences. That is why page 2's own digest below is a shorter page, and most of this file's interior_bytes drop. (2) At the 10.00 cm minimum storable trim -- not this book -- the structural TOC's eight rows and four 8.5 pt group gaps leave 47 px where the folio needs 49, so that page prints unnumbered. Neither is reachable from this card's own scope: G-1 forbids it the wording, the sizes' derivation and the layout, and G-6 forbids it CARD-205's 8.5 pt constant.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like with CARD-221's deterministic, packaged interior face in place. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, and an interior_bytes that no longer matches means the written file changed. If a card changes a page on purpose, it records its OWN new file under its own card number and says here what moved and why -- as this one does -- and leaves every earlier file in the chain alone.
interior_colorspace_note: What every page of this interior declares (CARD-147's own fact, unaffected by CARD-201). NOT the same as each page entry's 'mode' below, which is 'RGB' and always will be: that field is what tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages normalises every page to before digesting it, regardless of the file's own declared colour space.
font_dependent_pages_note:
EMPTY, AND THAT IS THIS CARD'S POINT: no interior page's pixels depend on the host any more, so there is no page for a reader of this fixture to skip. Every face the interior letters in now comes from data this repository ships -- _guide_face and _band_font both read src/nonogram/export/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf through importlib.resources (ADR-0006/R1: package data, not a dependency), and a puzzle page's clue digits come from Pillow's own embedded face, which was always on the machine-independent side of this line (see every predecessor's own note: 'the bundled band face and Pillow's built-in clue face, so their digests are comparable on any machine'). The field is kept as an explicit empty list rather than dropped so that this claim is stated where its predecessors stated the opposite, and so a future card that adds a host lookup has somewhere obvious to declare it.

The two fields that went with it are GONE from this file and from tests/helpers/book_corpus.py: font_fingerprint, font_fingerprint_note and MACHINE_FACE_SIZES. They existed because interior pixels depended on the host (CARD-146/CARD-147, the mechanism; CARD-149 and CARD-200 re-derived the tuple as sizes moved), and the measurement that retires them is the page-by-page comparison in why_a_new_baseline above plus the direct one in tests/test_book_interior_face.py, which exports this same book twice -- once with the host's Arial available and once with ImageFont.truetype made to refuse every host path -- and finds every page's digest, the page count and the chosen gutter band identical. Removing a gate whose condition still held would red the suite on someone's machine; this one's condition is measurably gone.

What is still host-dependent, and keeps no gate here because the interior baseline holds no page of it: BookPDFGenerator.create_cover_page still asks the host for Arial at 72 px for a GENERATED title cover. The cover is a separate file (INV-013: the interior holds no cover page), MACHINE_FACE_SIZES deliberately never covered its 72 px for that reason, and no baseline digests it -- so it is recorded in CARD-221's notes as work outside that card rather than gated here.
interior_bytes_note: The black-and-white interior of this book: 3464123 bytes, where CARD-205's recording held 3498430 (-34307, -0.98%) and this file's own pre-fix-1 recording held 3369113 (+95010). The seven lettered pages' JPEG streams are all re-encoded against CARD-205 (a different face is different high-frequency ink); the gain against this card's own earlier recording is almost all interior page 2, which prints its captions form again -- six more lines of text -- less the difficulty box's three sentences and its rule. The six pages that did not move contribute exactly 0 bytes of the difference from CARD-205, which is the same fact their unchanged digests state.
changed_pages_note: The seven pages lettered through _guide_face, and only those -- measured page by page against CARD-205's recording before this file was written, not predicted. Pages 1 and 2 are the guide (CARD-201's two-page tutorial; page 2 also drops a fallback level, see why_a_new_baseline), page 3 the structural table of contents (CARD-205's own page: its title and every row are set through _guide_face, so the rows are 49 px tall here against Arial's 48 and the title's line 258 px against 254), pages 4, 6 and 8 the Easy/Medium/Hard level dividers and page 10 the SOLUTIONS divider (one word each, at DIVIDER_PT). Pages 5, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 13 are byte-identical to CARD-205's: nothing this card touches letters them.
